The strongest public case rests on aggregate pass evidence plus general risk-management principles. But the admissible record also directly undercuts a clean-certification narrative: there is an unresolved named launch use case weakness, the model-card draft says no known material limitations, a reviewer already flagged whether this issue should be disclosed, and policy text says draft mitigations do not remove a current disclosure requirement unless approved with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. Because those elements are incomplete, support for certification without material caveat is weak. Private commercial pressure exists but is inadmissible and cannot support the public case.
